description: Initial structured privacy kinds. Domain assignments and format/context claims are project modeling facts awaiting sources; they are not source-backed yet. See docs/methodology/taxonomy.md.

kinds.label: Email address
openQuestions: RFC 5322 plain dot-atom addr-spec and RFC 5321 size limits are sourced; are quoted-string, domain-literal, obsolete and internationalized (RFC 6531, not read) forms in scope?
Which medical-context signals are sufficient for the phi domain to apply to an occurrence?

kinds.label: Telephone number
openQuestions: The E.164 recommendation text was not read (maximum length and structure unverified); which national forms are separate profiles?
Which jurisdiction-specific phone profiles are needed beyond the global profile?

kinds.label: Payment card number
openQuestions: Is a payment card number modeled as pii, as a separate financial domain, or both? The domain vocabulary currently has only pii and phi.

Length, prefix and check-digit claims rest on a secondary reference to ISO/IEC 7812 (not read); which issuer or standards documents settle them, and for which networks beyond Visa, Mastercard and American Express?
Under what circumstances does a payment made for health care make an occurrence phi?

kinds.label: International bank account number
openQuestions: Structure and check digits rest on a secondary reference; the registry (HTTP 403 when read) and ISO 13616 per-country structures are unread.
Is an account number of a legal entity within scope, and does its domain differ from a personal account?
Same open domain-vocabulary question as payment-card/global/basic.

kinds.label: United States Social Security number
openQuestions: SSA unassigned ranges were read only as search excerpts (direct fetch returned HTTP 403); direct reads of the SSA pages and the IRS ITIN publication are still needed.
Which labeled-field and unlabeled forms are separate profiles?

kinds.label: National or tax identifier (placeholder)
openQuestions: Which national and tax identifier families are worth modeling, and in which jurisdictions?
This entry only reserves the concept so that jurisdiction-dependent classification is representable; it is to be split into per-jurisdiction kinds, each with its own id, once researched.
Whether a given identifier is also phi depends on jurisdiction and context and is not established.

kinds.label: Medical record number
openQuestions: Which public-authority or provider-documented sources establish the health-domain role and the phi domain for this identifier?
Which field labels are documented, and does the structured value have any bounded format at all?
Are non-US profiles needed as separate ids?

Sources read state no value format (uniqueness is local to a set of medical records), so the identifier is recognized by label or type code. The label vocabulary is project-authored until a source lists labels. Holder-dependent applicability of the phi domain is not settled.

kinds.label: Health plan member identifier
openQuestions: Which sources document the identifier's role and field names?
Is the value structure bounded enough to describe, or is it only identifiable through its field label?

The sources read state no member id format; formats are carrier-specific. The Medicare Beneficiary Identifier has a CMS-documented format (claim phi-cms-mbi/format-and-randomness) and is a candidate separate kind, not modeled here.

kinds.label: Health insurance claim identifier
openQuestions: Is a claim identifier on its own a person-linked identifier, or only when joined with other data? Classification is not established.
The FHIR Claim resource links a patient through a separate required element, not through the identifier; the source read states no value format.
Domains listed are candidates pending that determination.

kinds.label: Prescription or order identifier
openQuestions: Is a prescription or order number on its own person-linked, or only joined with other data? Classification is not established.
The FHIR MedicationRequest resource links a subject through a separate element, not through the identifier; no pharmacy-standard source was read, so no format is stated.
Domains listed are candidates pending that determination.
